headline: COPPER HITS ALL-TIME COMEX RECORD: $14,802/T ($6.71/lb) — London Shortage Backwardation at Year's Widest as US Tariff Arbitrage Compounds Physical Squeeze
snippet: The September COMEX copper contract touched $6.7140 per pound ($14,802/t) on Wednesday August 13 — clearing the prior record of $6.7045 set August 5 — as a simultaneous physical shortage on the London Metal Exchange pushed the cash-to-three-month backwardation to its widest spread of 2026, with LME inventories falling to a five-month low as traders diverted metal to China. The dual signal — a new price record driven by US tariff-arbitrage pre-stockpiling AND a London shortage signalling non-US buyers are competing for the same material — is as strong a validation of the structural copper bull case as any sell-side price target, and directly reprices the NPV of North American copper development projects against inputs that were built on assumptions of $4–$5/lb copper.

headline: ARIZONA GOLD: 21.79m @ 4.10 g/t AU AT PHILADELPHIA — Perry Zone Extends 150m Vertically; BLM Permit Adds 16 New Drill Pads for Down-Dip Testing
source_name: Investing News Network / Arizona Gold & Silver Inc. (TSX-V: AZS)
snippet: Arizona Gold & Silver Inc. (TSX-V: AZS; OTCQB: AZASF) reported August 13 that drill hole PC26-169 at the Philadelphia Project in Arizona returned 21.79 metres at 4.10 g/t gold and 5.8 g/t silver within a broader 73.46-metre interval at 1.69 g/t gold — a result extending the Perry Zone approximately 150 metres vertically above prior high-grade intersections, confirming upward continuity of the gold-silver hydrothermal system along the Arabian Fault. A second hole (PC26-167) returned 15.24m at 2.66 g/t gold within 66.81m at 1.12 g/t gold, and an expanded US Bureau of Land Management permit adding 16 new drill pads has transitioned drilling to test the projected down-dip continuation of the high-grade core — the drill program remains active through 2026.

headline: GOLD BRIEFLY RECLAIMS $4,500 FOR FIRST TIME SINCE JANUARY — Flat July PPI Triggers Pullback to $4,349; Metal Now Consolidating at $4,376–$4,441
snippet: Gold futures briefly touched $4,500 per ounce on Wednesday August 12 — the first time that level has traded since January's $5,500 all-time high — before reversing sharply on Thursday when July PPI printed flat at 0.0% versus the 0.2% consensus and core PPI came in at +0.2% versus 0.3% expected, triggering profit-taking that sent spot gold to $4,349.80 (down 1.31%) and silver to $64.29 (down 1.40%). Gold is now consolidating in the $4,376–$4,441 range on Friday August 14, with the Fed's September rate pause probability at approximately 54% providing technical support; for junior gold mining investors, the $4,500 touch and orderly pullback confirms the structural breakout from the February–July falling wedge is intact rather than being reversed.

headline: LITHIUM IONIC EXITS SALINAS FOR US$37.5M CASH — Non-Dilutive Bandeira Construction Funding Secured; 2% Royalty Retained on PLS Brasil Spodumene Sales
snippet: Lithium Ionic Corp. (TSX-V: LTH) announced August 12 a definitive agreement to sell the Salinas group of lithium properties in Brazil's Lithium Valley to PLS Brasil Mineração Ltda. (wholly-owned subsidiary of ASX-listed PLS Group Limited) for US$30 million at closing plus a US$7.5 million contingent payment tied to a positive final investment decision at Colina or December 2029, while retaining a 2.0% net royalty on future spodumene concentrate sales from the Baixa Grande resource. Proceeds fund non-dilutive early works, procurement and construction-readiness activities at the 100%-owned Bandeira Lithium Project — allowing Lithium Ionic to concentrate capital on its flagship asset without equity dilution in a lithium market where project financing conditions have tightened relative to the mid-cycle highs of 2022–2023.

headline: DENISON Q2 SELLS 750,000 LBS URANIUM AT $122.16/LB — 233% Gain vs. Cost; Phoenix ISR Freeze Wall Installed at $700M Saskatchewan Build
source_name: PR Newswire / Denison Mines Corp. (TSX: DML; NYSE American: DNN)
snippet: Denison Mines Corp. (TSX: DML; NYSE: DNN) reported August 12 that Q2 2026 included the sale of 750,000 pounds of U3O8 at an average realized price of $122.16 per pound, generating $91.6 million in gross proceeds and a $64.1 million gain representing a 233% return from the uranium's original purchase price. On the construction front, installation of the Phase 1 perimeter freeze wall has been initiated at the Phoenix In-Situ Recovery Uranium Mine at Wheeler River, Saskatchewan — with over 20% of overall site civil work estimated complete and the $700 million (US$500 million) project on track for first production by mid-2028; Denison also holds 1.1 million pounds of physical uranium as of June 30, providing additional leverage to the uranium market structure.

headline: NORTHWEST COPPER KWANIKA PEA DUE IN WEEKS — 6,500m of 10,000m Drilled; Updated Economics to Reflect Current Copper Prices at Record Highs
snippet: NorthWest Copper Corp. (TSX-V: NWST) reported August 11 that its fully-funded 2026 exploration program at the Kwanika copper-gold project in north-central BC has completed over 6,500 metres of the targeted 10,000-metre campaign using three drill rigs targeting resource expansion and confidence upgrades in both the Western and open-pit Pit zones — with an updated Preliminary Economic Assessment incorporating the 2026 mineral resource expected in the coming weeks. For investors tracking imminent re-rating catalysts: a PEA update calculated against Comex copper at $14,802/t (versus lower copper price assumptions used in any prior study) will produce economics materially better than the prior benchmark, and the simultaneous release of new drill assays expected in late August/early September makes Kwanika one of the sector's most actionable dual-catalyst setups.

headline: MINING STOCKS GAIN $206 BILLION IN TWO WEEKS — Top 50 Companies Now Worth $2.17 Trillion; Gold and Silver Names Alone Add $108B in a Fortnight
snippet: Mining.com's analysis of the Top 50 largest mining companies shows their combined market capitalization rose from $2,169 billion to $2,375 billion over the most recent two weeks — a $206 billion gain — with gold and silver names accounting for $108 billion of the advance after bullion briefly touched $4,500 per ounce Wednesday, while copper and diversified names have collectively added $246 billion year-to-date for a 24% gain. The fortnight's concentration of value creation provides institutional validation of the sector's underlying earnings fundamentals: the top 50 are now generating their highest-ever free cash flow margins, yet their collective market capitalization — at $2.17 trillion — remains well below the implied NAV of their combined mineral reserves at current commodity prices, suggesting the re-rating thesis for the broader sector has further room to run.

headline: CHINA H2 RARE EARTH QUOTAS STILL UNPUBLISHED — 13 of 19 Tracked Elements Decline in August as Market Awaits Year's Biggest Single Catalyst
source_name: Canadian Mining Report / Rare Earth Mining
snippet: China has not published its second-half 2026 rare earth mining and smelting quotas — identified by market analysts as the single largest open catalyst for rare earth prices heading into September — even as August market data shows 13 of 19 tracked rare earth elements declining from July's levels, with gallium leading at -18.8% and only erbium posting meaningful gains at +17.6%, following China's Q2 quota-based price increases that reached approximately 45% quarter-over-quarter. For investors in ex-China rare earth developers: a reduced H2 quota would immediately tighten non-Chinese supply chains and increase strategic value of western processing capacity under Trump's Project Vault $12 billion Strategic Critical Minerals Reserve — making the delayed announcement the sector's most watched near-term price catalyst.

headline: AMERICAN PACIFIC DRILLING 15,000m AT MONTANA PORPHYRY — 2,048m Into Phase I as Madison Copper-Gold Skarn + Porphyry Assays Queue Up
source_name: Junior Mining Network / American Pacific Mining Corp. (CSE: USGD)
snippet: American Pacific Mining Corp. (CSE: USGD) reported August 13 that Phase I of its fully-funded 15,000-metre drill program at the Madison Copper-Gold Project in southwest Montana has completed 2,048 metres — 1,620 metres of diamond core targeting the primary porphyry system and 428 metres of reverse circulation holes testing near-surface skarn expressions and high-grade vein zones — with initial assay results expected in the coming weeks, followed by Phase II of approximately 5,000 additional metres. Madison is one of the few fully-funded, multi-technique copper-gold porphyry programs currently underway in the United States at a moment when domestic copper supply narratives command a structural premium in investor attention ahead of potential 2027 US refined copper import tariffs.

headline: GOLD ABOVE $4,500: 4 JUNIOR MINERS UNDER $45 THE MARKET HASN'T REPRICED YET
snippet: A new Yahoo Finance analysis identifies four junior gold mining stocks trading under $45 per share that carry significant re-rating potential at gold prices above $4,500 per ounce, with the thesis grounded in the mathematical disconnect between current equity prices and the NPV economics that current gold prices imply for projects with established resources, DFS-level studies, or near-production status. The analysis arrives as the sector's Q2 2026 reporting season has documented the widest P/E compression against earnings in the sector's modern history — majors reporting $3,000/oz gross margins at 13–20x earnings versus the 30–50x multiples that characterised prior gold cycles — creating an environment where smaller companies with similar margin leverage but institutional underweighting are the highest-beta opportunity for retail investors who entered before the re-rating.
